description: A junior Computer Science major with a strong interest in Cybersecurity who feels confident in high-level logic but struggles with manual memory management and low-level C debugging.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This node is included to ensure the student's some_prior_exposure tier is supported by a solid grasp of systems-level C before diving into kernel internals.
nodes.description: Foundational review of C programming constructs, specifically pointers and structures, as they apply to operating system kernel data.
nodes.title: C Systems Programming Refresher

nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard core requirement for block_01 to establish the boundary between hardware and software, tailored for a student with some_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: OS Services and Kernel Modes
nodes.description: Introduction to the fundamental roles of an operating system, focusing on the distinction between user mode and kernel mode operations.
Exploration of the system call interface and the various architectural structures of modern operating systems (monolithic, layered, microkernel).
nodes.title: System Calls and OS Architecture
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required content to complete the foundation of block_01, ensuring the student with some_prior_exposure understands how applications request OS services.
Core requirement for block_02; builds on the foundations of block_01 to define how programs execute.
nodes.title: Process Lifecycle and Control Blocks
nodes.description: Detailed look at the process abstraction, including the Process Control Block (PCB) and the state transitions in a process lifecycle.
Comparison of Inter-Process Communication (IPC) techniques, including shared memory and message passing through sockets.
nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication Mechanisms
nodes.personalizationRationale: Necessary core node for block_02 covering how separate processes exchange data in a multi-tasking environment.
Essential core content for block_03, transitioning from heavy-weight processes to light-weight execution units.
nodes.description: Analysis of threading models (many-to-one, one-to-one) and the implementation of threading libraries like Pthreads.
nodes.title: Threading Models and Libraries

nodes.description: Evaluation of CPU scheduling algorithms including Round Robin, FCFS, and Priority Scheduling based on specific criteria.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms
nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard block_03 core topic focusing on the analytical modeling of CPU efficiency and throughput.
Leverages the student's some_prior_exposure to investigate advanced scheduling scenarios beyond the standard core curriculum.
nodes.title: Advanced Real-Time Scheduling Considerations
nodes.description: Deep dive into Real-Time Scheduling and the performance trade-offs of Multi-Core Processor Scheduling.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory assessment checkpoint for the midterm, ensuring all foundational concepts are mastered by the some_prior_exposure student.
nodes.description: A comprehensive review of chapters 1 through 5, preparing for the week-8 midterm exam.
nodes.title: Midterm Exam Review (Ch 1-5)
The Critical Section and Mutexes
nodes.description: Introduction to the critical section problem and the use of Mutex locks to ensure mutual exclusion in concurrent code.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core block_04 content, vital for the synchronization project; builds directly on the student's previous threading knowledge.

nodes.title: Semaphores and Classic Sync Problems
nodes.description: Advanced synchronization tools including Semaphores and Monitors, illustrated via the Dining Philosophers problem.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Final core requirement for block_04, covering synchronization primitives frequently tested on the final exam.

nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization and Prevention
nodes.description: Analysis of the four necessary conditions for deadlock and strategies for prevention and avoidance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required floor block content for block_05, scaled to address mandatory deadlock characterization concepts.

nodes.description: Examination of physical memory allocation, including contiguous allocation and the mechanics of paging and page tables.
nodes.title: Address Mapping and Paging Structures
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core node for block_06, providing the necessary theory for memory management project implementation.
Critical core topic for block_06 that connects theoretical paging to practical system performance and thrashing.
nodes.title: Virtual Memory and Page Replacement
nodes.description: Study of Virtual Memory, demand paging, and page replacement algorithms such as LRU and Optimal.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential core material for the final block_07, covering the interaction between the OS and peripheral hardware.
nodes.title: I/O Systems and Hardware Interfaces
nodes.description: Overview of I/O system architectures, hardware interfaces, and the role of the I/O subsystem in OS performance.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Final core instructional node covering the storage management requirements of the block_07 capstone.
nodes.description: Implementation details of file systems, including disk block allocation and directory structures.
nodes.title: File System Implementation Strategy
Final Cumulative Review Exam Prep
nodes.description: Cumulative review session covering all course material from OS foundations through file systems to prepare for the final exam.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory final review assessment to ensure the student with some_prior_exposure is prepared for the 40% cumulative final.
